title: They Gave You Life
text:
They gave you life and now you live

even beyond their desires.

You were for them a necessary chimera

and you take possession of your owners.


And we will not say you do not exist

though tenaciously we deny you:

if in the desert of their life

your dreamed kingdoms are only mirages,

in our mind you are, you are, perhaps

more than we are, you are certain.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradox of an invented being becoming more certain than its makers.

title: Outside the Voice...
text:
Outside the voice

perhaps an offering

more living and vehement

than the burning memory

that clenches in my arms.


Embers of light fall

from a tormented sky.

Will they be at last

contours of love

so long awaited

for a real world?


Obsessed with the question I am.

To exist through words,

insolent vocation.




1974
editorial_note: The translation keeps the difficult opening and the final vocation to exist through words.

title: Companion of Today
text:
Companion of today, I want

no truth other than yours, to live

where your eyes grow,

giving your light, your channel

to what I see and feel...


Undo that dark skein

of fear,

find what was lost,

break the voice of sleep...


And slowly, slowly

learn to live,

again, again,

as on a morning

loaded with wealth.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the intimate address as a patient relearning of life.

title: Excessive Passion, Furious Longings
text:
Excessive passion, furious longings

for you, longings for nothing!

Stubborn spring opposed you,

but spring was ending.

Stubborn we beside our books,

Spanish poets, deaf Spain!

Against the dark stone of your centuries,

the fleetingness of the word.

Excessive passion for you,

mistaken passion of love!




1966
editorial_note: The translation keeps the address to Spain and the fleetingness of the word against history.

title: Everything Is Inevitable. Drowning the Light There Rises...
text:
Everything is inevitable. Drowning the light there rises,

powerful and tenacious, the nightmare.

In the light body heaviness beats:

a sea of shadows overflows

from the immortal shore to our shore.

But I write verses in search of clarities.


And knowing the faith of my verse, without hesitating I affirm

the absolute meaning of life

on a meaningless earth.




1951
editorial_note: The translation keeps the affirmative claim of meaning on a meaningless earth.

title: These Nights of Rain I Hear Them on the Panes...
text:
These rainy nights I hear them on the panes,

these windy nights and I cannot move.


At the door of fear the guard keeps watch,

child prisoner, lest he be unchained.


Other nights of deep rain on the panes,

other nights of wind and I question again.


Because everything was useless I have changed masters,

at the door of sleep, lady of clarity.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the guarded fear and the final turn toward sleep as a new master.

title: From Night to Night
text:
From night to night higher it seemed

in burning memory the tree of dreams,

as if you held the fire of our life,

the power of a bonfire.


So many, many times

of this unreal world, prisoner and hostage,

with what hope today I see the most vivid contour

of the day, the reality of a moment,

with what avidity, with what fervor I distinguish

the voice, the hand, the breast.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the movement from unreal captivity into vivid bodily reality.

title: If These Verses of Today at Least Were...
text:
If these verses of today at least were

an arch of concord, a future language,

but no, cowardice, terror

—if not pure stupidity—

drive me to write

what no one and nobody expects.


From the bird or the child or the sea,

from the syllableless prisoner,

from the mutism of the mute,

from the dog's bark

perhaps the contact poem will arise,

the serene sound, free lucidity.




1974
editorial_note: The translation keeps the search for a future language in nonhuman or broken speech.

title: About What I Love Most
text:
Over what I love most, over my own things,

your law and your power impose themselves.

Years ago, years now in distance,

from my own dwelling someone who is not I,

the most secret keys offered you.

You kept them, they remain

still unrecovered.


...And flames of dread rise

inside the heart on these cold nights:

when you come stealthily,

when you brutally force me to yourself.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the image of secret keys surrendered by an estranged self.

title: The Limits
text:
I think of my limits,

limits that separate

the poem I make

from the one I cannot make,

the poem I write

from the one I will never be able to write.

Limits also, consequently,

of what I love

and what I will never be able to love.


Limits of what I would like to say

or see or have.

Words I would give

to discover, words to help.

Limits of love, words

insufficiently valuable,

in an endless desert.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the equation between poetic limits and limits of love.
